title: Solvable and unsolvable instances of the equal sum partition problem
summary: We consider the equal sum partition problem, motivated by distance magic graph labeling: Given $n,k \in \N$ such that $k\, | \sum_{i=1}^ni$ and a partition $p_1+\cdots+p_k=n$, when is it possible to find a partition of the set $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ into $k$ subsets of sizes $p_1,\dots,p_k$, such that the element sum in each subset is the same? A known necessary condition is the \emph{slack condition}, requiring that for all $j$, placing the largest possible elements in the $j$ smallest sets yields a total sum that is at least what is needed.
